import { Code } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'
import client from '../../../../snippets/client.ts?raw'
import react from '../../../../snippets/react.tsx?raw'

`@familiar-ai/client` connects to the HTTP API, mirrors everything the event stream sends and derives a transcript a chat UI can render. Familiar's own web app is built on it.

```sh
npm install @familiar-ai/client
```

## The store

<Code code={client} lang="ts" title="client.ts" />

`createFamiliarStore(url, options)` opens the event stream straight away. The store offers every command; one your host's [`allow`](/familiar/build/serve-the-api/#decide-who-may-do-what) refuses rejects with its 403, so render only the UI each person may use. The optional `fetch` makes every request, including stream reconnects, so you can attach a fresh credential each time. An open stream keeps the credentials it started with until it reconnects.

The store's state is plain data from the event stream. Read it with `getState()` and `subscribe()`:

- `view` and `history`: the live conversation and the older entries loaded before it
- `transcript`: the derived chat items and whether a run is `busy`
- `memory`, `episodes` and `schedules`: the streamed documents, under their wire names
- `account`: the streamed sign-in state

Change things by calling the commands on the store itself, grouped as `store.conversation`, `store.memory`, `store.schedules`, `store.account`, `store.push`, `store.connections` and `store.mcp`. They never change identity, so you can pass them around freely.

Streamed documents are `undefined` until they arrive, and `null` when the server sends none.

`send(text)` posts a message with a fresh `requestId`. The host decides who sent it.

## The transcript

`state.transcript.items` is what a chat shows, in order. Each item has an `id` that stays the same across updates. Use it as the key.

- `message`: a person's words, with their `author`, and `queued` while it waits for the current run
- `reply`: Familiar's `text`, `thinking` and `toolCalls`, with `streaming`, `stopped` and any `error`
- `scheduled`: a schedule's prompt arriving, with its `due` time and `creator`
- `waiting`: a run has started but nothing is visible yet
- `compaction`: older messages were summarised for the model here

Each tool call has a `name`, `arguments`, `status` (`running`, `done` or `error`), text `output` and optional `details`. `details` is whatever the tool returned for UIs. Narrow it before you render it.

Older entries arrive through `store.conversation.loadOlder()`. `state.history.status` is `more`, `loading`, `failed` or `start`.

## The connection

`state.connection` moves through these values:

| Value          | Meaning                                                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `connecting`   | The first stream request is under way                                          |
| `open`         | A compatible protocol handshake and full view have arrived                     |
| `reconnecting` | A network error, closed stream, 5xx or 429. The store retries with fresh state |
| `unauthorized` | The stream was answered 401 or 403. Retries stop                               |
| `failed`       | Any other unusable answer, such as a 404. Retries stop                         |
| `outdated`     | The protocol handshake was missing or incompatible. Retries stop               |

The store never reloads the page or signs anyone in. After a terminal state, sign-out or an identity change, call `store.disconnect()` and create a new store. Commands reject with the server's error and aren't retried. Commands already sent still settle after you disconnect.

## React

Install React 18 or 19, then use the separate `/react` entry:

<Code code={react} lang="tsx" title="App.tsx" />

Create the store once, outside render, where your app manages connections. `FamiliarProvider` gives its subtree a store, and nested providers each give their own. The provider doesn't open or close it. `useFamiliar` compares selections with `Object.is`, so return stable values such as a single field. `useFamiliarStore()` returns the nearest provider's store, for its commands. The vanilla entry doesn't load React.
